# MLS-Bench: theory-semiautomata

# theory-semiautomata

## Research Question
Which **parallel-time architecture** (and AdamW recipe) best *learns* to
simulate hard finite-state semiautomata — word problems of non-solvable
permutation groups — from state supervision on short words, so that the
learned simulation keeps working on words much longer than any seen in
training, within a fixed online-training budget? Sequentially-recurrent
models are excluded by construction (see below): for them the task is
trivial, so the open research question lives entirely in the parallel-time
regime.

## Background
Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy & Zhang, "Transformers Learn Shortcuts to
Automata" (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.10749) show that shallow non-recurrent
networks learn shortcut solutions to semiautomata that fail out of
distribution. Simulating a non-solvable group is **NC1-complete**
(Barrington, JCSS 1989), so no constant-depth model expresses it unless
TC0 = NC1, and Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of State in
State-Space Models" (ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove diagonal linear
recurrences (the Mamba/GLA family) sit in TC0. The current frontier changes
the structure of the linear recurrence's state-transition matrix: negative
eigenvalues (Grazzi et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv:2411.12537), products of
generalized Householder transformations (Siems et al., NeurIPS 2025,
arXiv:2502.10297), and sparse permutation-times-diagonal transitions
(Terzic et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2509.22284). The environments are the
non-solvable group word problems of Terzic et al.: each letter is one of a
redundant set of generating permutations, and the target at every position
is the running product, i.e. the current group element.

**Why recurrent models are excluded.** NC1-hardness constrains only
models whose serial depth does not grow with sequence length. A sequential
RNN simulates *any* finite automaton by construction (Liu et al. Fig. 5;
Merrill et al. Fig. 3), so it is the excluded skyline, not a baseline. Two
FIXED runtime guards enforce this structurally: a module scan (no
`nn.LSTM/GRU/RNN/*Cell`) and an autograd serial-depth probe (the longest
backward-graph path at length 1024 may exceed the one at length 256 by at
most 80 nodes). Log-depth associative scans, attention, and convolutions
all pass; per-token recurrence fails.

## Environments
Three word problems of non-solvable groups (S5 and A5) that differ in the
group and in how many redundant generating permutations make up the
alphabet. Training draws fresh words every step; per-position
cross-entropy on the state sequence; AdamW with the agent-chosen recipe.

## Metric
State accuracy on held-out words longer than the training words. The
per-environment `score` rescales accuracy so chance (1/|Q|) pins to 0; raw
`test_accuracy` stays as a diagnostic. The task score combines the
environments by a fixed rule.

## Baselines
- **transformer** — depth-1 GPT-2-style Transformer (Liu et al. 2023
  App. B.3: d=512, MLP 512, 8 heads); the shallow floor and the starter.
- **transformer_deep** — the same at depth 8.
- **looped_transformer** — one weight-shared block applied 8 times
  (Giannou et al. 2023).
- **diag_ssm** — gated diagonal linear recurrence with a log-depth parallel
  scan (Mamba family; eigenvalues in (0, 1)).
- **mamba_neg** — Mamba with the state-transition eigenvalue range extended
  to (-1, 1), 5 layers (Grazzi et al. 2025).
- **deltanet_neg** — DeltaNet with beta in [0, 2] (eigenvalues in [-1, 1]),
  5 layers (Grazzi et al. 2025).
- **deltaproduct** — DeltaProduct with 4 generalized Householder
  transformations per token and eigenvalues in [-1, 1], one layer
  (Siems et al. 2025).
- **pd_ssm** — PD-SSM: input-dependent column-one-hot permutation times
  complex diagonal transition, one layer (Terzic et al. 2025).

   279: def _graph_depth(output: torch.Tensor) -> int:

   286:     while stack:
   287:         node = stack[-1]
   288:         if node in depth:
   289:             stack.pop()
   290:             continue
   291:         pending = [
   292:             child
   293:             for child, _ in node.next_functions
   294:             if child is not None and child not in depth
   295:         ]
   296:         if pending:
   297:             stack.extend(pending)

   300:             for child, _ in node.next_functions:

   379: 
   380:     def __init__(self, d_model: int):

   383:         self.a_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)

   385:         self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)

   387:     def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   388:         u = self.norm(x)
   389:         a = torch.sigmoid(self.a_proj(u))       # decay gate in (0, 1)
   390:         h = (1.0 - a) * self.v_proj(u)          # input contribution
   391:         # Inclusive Hillis-Steele scan: ceil(log2 T) combine rounds, each a
   392:         # constant number of parallel ops, so serial depth is O(log T).
   393:         T = x.shape[1]

   397:             h_prev = F.pad(h, (0, 0, offset, 0), value=0.0)[:, :T]

import argparse
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import torch.optim as optim
from torchvision import datasets, transforms
from torch.optim.lr_scheduler import StepLR


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(Net, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 32, 3, 1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, 1)
        self.dropout1 = nn.Dropout(0.25)
        self.dropout2 = nn.Dropout(0.5)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(9216, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, 10)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        x = F.relu(x)
        x = self.conv2(x)
        x = F.relu(x)
        x = F.max_pool2d(x, 2)
        x = self.dropout1(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.fc1(x)
        x = F.relu(x)
        x = self.dropout2(x)
        x = self.fc2(x)
        output = F.log_softmax(x, dim=1)
        return output


def train(args, model, device, train_loader, optimizer, epoch):
    model.train()
    for batch_idx, (data, target) in enumerate(train_loader):
        data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        output = model(data)
        loss = F.nll_loss(output, target)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        if batch_idx % args.log_interval == 0:
            print('Train Epoch: {} [{}/{} ({:.0f}%)]\tLoss: {:.6f}'.format(
                epoch, batch_idx * len(data), len(train_loader.dataset),
                100. * batch_idx / len(train_loader), loss.item()))
            if args.dry_run:
                break


def test(model, device, test_loader):
    model.eval()
    test_loss = 0
    correct = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for data, target in test_loader:
            data, target = data.to(device), target.to(device)
            output = model(data)
            test_loss += F.nll_loss(output, target, reduction='sum').item()  # sum up batch loss
            pred = output.argmax(dim=1, keepdim=True)  # get the index of the max log-probability
            correct += pred.eq(target.view_as(pred)).sum().item()

    test_loss /= len(test_loader.dataset)

    print('\nTest set: Average loss: {:.4f}, Accuracy: {}/{} ({:.0f}%)\n'.format(
        test_loss, correct, len(test_loader.dataset),
        100. * correct / len(test_loader.dataset)))


def main():
    # Training settings
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='PyTorch MNIST Example')
    parser.add_argument('--batch-size', type=int, default=64, metavar='N',
                        help='input batch size for training (default: 64)')
    parser.add_argument('--test-batch-size', type=int, default=1000, metavar='N',
                        help='input batch size for testing (default: 1000)')
    parser.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=14, metavar='N',
                        help='number of epochs to train (default: 14)')
    parser.add_argument('--lr', type=float, default=1.0, metavar='LR',
                        help='learning rate (default: 1.0)')
    parser.add_argument('--gamma', type=float, default=0.7, metavar='M',

    parser.add_argument('--no-accel', action='store_true',
                        help='disables accelerator')
    parser.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true',
                        help='quickly check a single pass')
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=1, metavar='S',
                        help='random seed (default: 1)')
    parser.add_argument('--log-interval', type=int, default=10, metavar='N',
                        help='how many batches to wait before logging training status')
    parser.add_argument('--save-model', action='store_true', 
                        help='For Saving the current Model')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    use_accel = not args.no_accel and torch.cuda.is_available()

    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)

    if use_accel:

    else:
        device = torch.device("cpu")

    train_kwargs = {'batch_size': args.batch_size}
    test_kwargs = {'batch_size': args.test_batch_size}
    if use_accel:

Research question: which **parallel-time architecture** (and AdamW recipe)
best LEARNS to simulate hard finite-state semiautomata from full state
supervision, within a fixed online-training budget?

The setup is in the spirit of Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy & Zhang,
"Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata" (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.10749):
online training with a freshly drawn batch at every step, AdamW, and a
per-position cross-entropy on the full state sequence. Their headline
finding: shallow non-recurrent networks learn o(T)-depth "shortcuts" to
solvable semiautomata, but accuracy on non-solvable word problems climbs
slowly with depth.

Simulating a non-solvable group is NC1-complete (Barrington, JCSS 1989),
so no constant-depth parallel model can express it (unless TC0 = NC1), and
Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of State in State-Space Models"
(ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove diagonal linear recurrences (S4/Mamba
family) sit in L-uniform TC0 — they need depth growing with T on exactly
this problem.

IMPORTANT — why recurrent models are excluded here: NC1-hardness only
constrains models whose serial computation depth does not grow with T.
A sequential RNN simulates ANY finite automaton by construction; both
reference papers use it as the trivial skyline (Liu et al. Fig. 5: a
1-layer LSTM reaches 100% on every task; Merrill et al. Fig. 3: a 1-layer
RNN solves every word problem). The open research question lives entirely
in the parallel-time regime, so this scaffold enforces it structurally
with two FIXED runtime guards that are *measured*, never self-reported:

  1. a module scan rejecting `nn.LSTM / nn.GRU / nn.RNN / *Cell` instances;
  2. an autograd-graph serial-depth probe: the longest path in the backward
     graph at seq_len 1024 may exceed the one at seq_len 256 by at most 80
     nodes. Per-token (or fine-grained chunkwise) python recurrences fail;
     attention, convolutions, and log-depth associative scans pass.

The transition tables are driver-private (`_PRIVATE_TABLES`) and the
automaton seed is masked before editable code sees the config: the model
must LEARN the automaton from sampled (input, state) streams. Hard-coding
or reconstructing any transition table inside the editable block is out of
contract, and an init-time tripwire aborts any run whose *untrained* model
already beats 25% accuracy (chance is at most 1/24).

The editable region exposes three functions:
  1. `build_model(env_spec, config)` returns an `nn.Module` mapping a token
     id sequence `[B, T]` to per-position state logits `[B, T, Q]`.
  2. `get_optimizer_config(config)` returns AdamW hyperparameters.
  3. `forward_logits(model, input_ids, env_spec)` is the inference wrapper.

def sinusoidal_table(max_len: int, d_model: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Fixed sinusoidal positional encodings (Vaswani et al. 2017).

    A standard choice for this family of experiments; shared here so every
    architecture can reuse it.
    """
    position = torch.arange(max_len, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
    div = torch.exp(
        torch.arange(0, d_model, 2, dtype=torch.float32)
        * (-math.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )
    table = torch.zeros(max_len, d_model)
    table[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div)
    table[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div[: d_model // 2])
    return table

# Driver-private transition tables, keyed by env name. Reading, copying, or
# reconstructing these from the editable block is OUT OF CONTRACT: the model
# must learn the automaton from the sampled (input, state) streams alone.
_PRIVATE_TABLES: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}


# Liu et al. 2023, App. B.1.1: "The generator set for S_n consists of the
# minimal generators, a transposition and an n-cycle, as well as 6 other
# permutations ... chosen following the ordering given by the
# sympy.combinatorics package". The "6 other" are the first six
# elements of `SymmetricGroup(n).generate()` (sympy 1.14) that are neither the
# identity nor one of the two minimal generators, frozen here so the image
# needs no sympy. Permutations are array forms: p[i] is the image of i.
_GROUP_ALPHABETS: dict[str, list[tuple[int, ...]]] = {
    "s4_word": [(1, 0, 2, 3), (1, 2, 3, 0),            # (1 2), (1 2 3 4)
                (2, 3, 0, 1), (3, 1, 2, 0), (0, 2, 3, 1),
                (1, 3, 0, 2), (2, 0, 1, 3), (3, 2, 0, 1)],
    "s5_word": [(1, 0, 2, 3, 4), (1, 2, 3, 4, 0),      # (1 2), (1 2 3 4 5)
                (0, 1, 4, 2, 3), (1, 2, 0, 3, 4), (2, 3, 1, 4, 0),
                (3, 4, 2, 0, 1), (4, 1, 0, 2, 3), (0, 2, 3, 1, 4)],
}


def _group_word(config: TaskConfig) -> tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]:
    """A symmetric-group word problem of Liu et al. 2023 (App. B.1.1).

    States are the elements of the group the letters generate (all n! permutations
    for these generator sets), sorted lexicographically, identity first (state 0).
    The state is the running left-product g_t = a_t o g_{t-1} from the identity,
    and each letter a_t is drawn uniformly from the paper's generator set. S4 is
    solvable (constant-depth shortcuts exist, Liu et al. Thm. 2); S5 is not: its
    word problem is NC1-complete (Barrington 1989) and Merrill et al. 2024 prove
    it inexpressible by diagonal SSMs.
    """
    name = config.env_name
    alphabet = _GROUP_ALPHABETS[name]
    n = len(alphabet[0])

    def compose(p: tuple[int, ...], q: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        # (p o q)(i) = p[q[i]] -- apply q first, then p.
        return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(n))

    # the group the letters generate (all of S_n, A_n, ...), sorted, identity first
    identity = tuple(range(n))
    seen, frontier = {identity}, [identity]
    while frontier:
        nxt = []
        for g in frontier:
            for a in alphabet:
                h = compose(a, g)
                if h not in seen:
                    seen.add(h)
                    nxt.append(h)
        frontier = nxt
    elements = sorted(seen)
    index = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(elements)}

    Q, Sigma = len(elements), len(alphabet)
    delta = torch.zeros(Q, Sigma, dtype=torch.long)
    for qi, elem in enumerate(elements):
        for ai, a in enumerate(alphabet):
            delta[qi, ai] = index[compose(a, elem)]
    spec = EnvSpec(
        name=name,
        alphabet_size=Sigma,
        num_states=Q,
        seq_len=config.seq_len,
        max_len=max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )
    return spec, delta


_ENV_BUILDERS: dict[str, Callable[[TaskConfig], tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]]] = {
    "s4_word": _group_word,
    "s5_word": _group_word,
}


def build_env_spec(config: TaskConfig) -> EnvSpec:
    if config.env_name not in _ENV_BUILDERS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown env {config.env_name!r}")
    spec, delta = _ENV_BUILDERS[config.env_name](config)
    _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name] = delta
    return spec


def sample_batch(spec: EnvSpec, batch_size: int, length: int,
                 generator: torch.Generator) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Walk the (private) transition table from state 0 for `length` steps."""
    delta = _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name]
    inputs = torch.randint(
        0, spec.alphabet_size, (batch_size, length),
        generator=generator, dtype=torch.long,
    )
    cur = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.long)
    states = torch.zeros(batch_size, length, dtype=torch.long)
    for t in range(length):
        cur = delta[cur, inputs[:, t]]
        states[:, t] = cur
    return inputs, states


def normalize_optimizer_config(cfg: dict[str, float]) -> OptimizerConfig:
    required = {"lr", "wd", "beta1", "beta2"}
    missing = required - set(cfg)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing optimizer hyperparameters: {sorted(missing)}")
    out = OptimizerConfig(
        lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
        wd=float(cfg["wd"]),
        beta1=float(cfg["beta1"]),
        beta2=float(cfg["beta2"]),
    )
    if out.lr <= 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW learning rate must be positive.")
    if out.wd < 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW weight decay must be non-negative.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta1 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta1 must satisfy 0 < beta1 < 1.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta2 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta2 must satisfy 0 < beta2 < 1.")
    return out

_FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT = (nn.LSTM, nn.GRU, nn.RNN, nn.RNNBase,
                        nn.LSTMCell, nn.GRUCell, nn.RNNCell)


def check_no_recurrent_modules(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    for mod in model.modules():
        if isinstance(mod, _FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Recurrent module {type(mod).__name__} detected. This task "
                f"restricts the design space to parallel-time architectures: "
                f"a sequential RNN simulates any finite automaton by "
                f"construction (Liu et al. 2023 Fig. 5 report a 1-layer LSTM "
                f"at 100% on every task), so it is the excluded skyline here."
            )


def _graph_depth(output: torch.Tensor) -> int:
    """Longest path length in the autograd graph rooted at `output`."""
    root = output.grad_fn
    if root is None:
        return 0
    depth: dict = {}
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack[-1]
        if node in depth:
            stack.pop()
            continue
        pending = [
            child
            for child, _ in node.next_functions
            if child is not None and child not in depth
        ]
        if pending:
            stack.extend(pending)
        else:
            best = 0
            for child, _ in node.next_functions:
                if child is not None:
                    best = max(best, depth[child])
            depth[node] = 1 + best
            stack.pop()
    return depth[root]


def check_serial_depth(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                       config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Reject architectures whose serial depth grows with sequence length.

    Two dummy batches (lengths depth_probe_short and depth_probe_long) are
    forwarded and the longest autograd paths compared. Constant-depth models
    (attention, convolutions) and log-depth associative scans pass; per-token
    python recurrences add thousands of serial nodes and fail.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.train()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    depths = []
    for probe_len in (config.depth_probe_short, config.depth_probe_long):
        tokens = torch.randint(
            0, env_spec.alphabet_size, (2, probe_len),
            generator=gen, dtype=torch.long,
        ).to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, tokens, env_spec)
        depths.append(_graph_depth(logits))
    model.train(was_training)
    short_d, long_d = depths
    if long_d > short_d + config.depth_slack:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Serial-depth guard: autograd depth grew from {short_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_short}) to {long_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_long}); allowed slack is "
            f"{config.depth_slack}. Sequentially-recurrent computation is "
            f"not admissible in this task."
        )
    print(
        f"DEPTH_PROBE short={short_d} long={long_d} slack={config.depth_slack}",
        flush=True,
    )


@torch.no_grad()
def check_init_tripwire(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                        config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Abort if the *untrained* model already simulates the automaton.

    Chance accuracy is at most 1/24; an untrained learned model sits near
    chance, while a hard-coded (or table-reading) simulator is near 1.0.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20240819)
    correct, total = 0, 0
    for _ in range(4):
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, config.seq_len, gen)
        xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
        preds = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec).argmax(dim=-1)
        correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
        total += yb.numel()
    model.train(was_training)
    acc = correct / max(total, 1)
    print(f"INIT_TRIPWIRE acc={acc:.6f} threshold={config.init_tripwire_acc}",
          flush=True)
    if acc >= config.init_tripwire_acc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Init tripwire: untrained model reaches accuracy {acc:.4f} "
            f">= {config.init_tripwire_acc} (chance <= 1/24). Hard-coding "
            f"the automaton instead of learning it is out of contract."
        )

class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Default baseline: shallow GPT-2-style Transformer.

    Follows Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3: embedding dim 512, MLP width 512,
    8 heads, sinusoidal positional encodings; depth 1 is their shallowest
    configuration. Maps token ids [B, T] to state logits [B, T, Q].
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, n_heads: int = 8, n_layers: int = 1,
                 dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.register_buffer(
            "pos_table", sinusoidal_table(max_len, d_model), persistent=False)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=d_model,
            dropout=dropout, batch_first=True, activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)
        mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(max_len, max_len), diagonal=1).bool()
        self.register_buffer("causal_mask", mask, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids) + self.pos_table[:T].unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.encoder(x, mask=self.causal_mask[:T, :T], is_causal=True)
        return self.head(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the sequence model. Output: [B, T, num_states] logits."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        n_heads=8,
        n_layers=1,
        dropout=0.0,
    )

                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Run the model on `input_ids` and return logits [B, T, num_states]."""
    return model(input_ids)

def evaluate(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
             device: torch.device, eval_seed: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    correct, total, loss_sum = 0, 0, 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                                  config.seq_len, gen)
            xb = xb.to(device)
            yb = yb.to(device)
            logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                yb.reshape(-1),
            )
            preds = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
            total += yb.numel()
            loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return correct / max(total, 1), loss_sum / max(total, 1)


EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS = 4096   # 16 words x 256 tokens


def evaluate_lengths(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
                     protocol: LengthProtocol, device: torch.device,
                     eval_seed: int) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Accuracy on fresh words whose length is drawn per batch from
    U[eval_len_min, eval_len_max]: over all positions and at the final one."""
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    len_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed + 1)
    c_all = t_all = c_fin = t_fin = 0
    loss_sum = 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            length = int(torch.randint(protocol.eval_len_min,
                                       protocol.eval_len_max + 1, (1,),
                                       generator=len_gen))
            xb_all, yb_all = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, length, gen)
            # Memory only: long words are forwarded in sequence chunks of at most
            # EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS tokens (words are independent; same words, same
            # order, same counts). Lengths <= 256 are never chunked.
            step = max(1, EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS // length)
            for i in range(0, xb_all.shape[0], step):
                xb = xb_all[i:i + step].to(device)
                yb = yb_all[i:i + step].to(device)
                logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
                loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                                       yb.reshape(-1))
                hit = logits.argmax(dim=-1) == yb
                c_all += hit.sum().item()
                t_all += yb.numel()
                c_fin += hit[:, -1].sum().item()
                t_fin += yb.shape[0]
                loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return {"acc_all": c_all / max(t_all, 1), "acc_final": c_fin / max(t_fin, 1),
            "loss": loss_sum / max(t_all, 1)}


def normalize_recipe(cfg: dict, config: TaskConfig) -> dict:
    """Optional training-recipe keys of `get_optimizer_config`'s dict.

    Defaults reproduce the plain recipe (constant lr, clip at
    `config.max_grad_norm`, one AdamW group), so a dict without these keys
    trains exactly as before. Keys:
      lr_schedule: "constant" | "warmup_cosine" (linear warmup over
                   warmup_frac * train_steps, then cosine to final_lr at the
                   last step; warmup_frac = 0 is torch's CosineAnnealingLR
                   with eta_min = final_lr)
      warmup_frac: float in [0, 1)            final_lr: float >= 0
      max_grad_norm: float > 0, or None for no clipping
      no_decay: list of parameter-name substrings trained with weight decay 0
    The step budget, batch size and evaluation are fixed.
    """
    schedule = cfg.get("lr_schedule", "constant")
    if schedule not in ("constant", "warmup_cosine"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown lr_schedule {schedule!r}.")
    warmup_frac = float(cfg.get("warmup_frac", 0.0))
    final_lr = float(cfg.get("final_lr", 0.0))
    if not 0.0 <= warmup_frac < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("warmup_frac must lie in [0, 1).")
    if final_lr < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("final_lr must be non-negative.")
    clip = cfg.get("max_grad_norm", config.max_grad_norm)
    if clip is not None:
        clip = float(clip)
        if clip <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError("max_grad_norm must be positive (or None).")
    no_decay = [str(s) for s in cfg.get("no_decay", ())]
    return {"lr_schedule": schedule, "warmup_frac": warmup_frac,
            "final_lr": final_lr, "max_grad_norm": clip,
            "no_decay": no_decay}


def scheduled_lr(step: int, total: int, max_lr: float, recipe: dict) -> float:
    """Learning rate for the optimizer step with 0-based index `step`."""

    min_lr = recipe["final_lr"]

    if step >= total:

    if args.batch_size is not None:

        train_len_min=args.train_len_min, eval_len_min=args.eval_len_min,
        eval_len_max=args.eval_len_max, metric=args.eval_metric,
        early_stop=not args.no_early_stop)

        raise ValueError("--eval-len-min and --eval-len-max go together.")

            1 <= protocol.eval_len_min <= protocol.eval_len_max
            <= max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long)):
        raise ValueError("eval lengths must satisfy 1 <= min <= max <= max_len.")
    if protocol.train_len_min is not None and not (
            1 <= protocol.train_len_min <= config.seq_len):
        raise ValueError("--train-len-min must lie in [1, seq_len].")

    env_spec = build_env_spec(config)
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        f"env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"batch={config.batch_size} steps={config.train_steps} "
        f"eval_batches={config.eval_batches} seed={config.seed}",
        flush=True,
    )

    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(f"{k}={v:.6f}" for k, v in metrics.items()),
        flush=True,

                   for k in ("acc_all", "acc_final", "acc_train_len") if k in metrics)
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS[{nonce}] test_accuracy={metrics['test_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"score={metrics['score']:.6f}{diag}",
        flush=True,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"

                "num_states": env_spec.num_states,
                "seq_len": env_spec.seq_len,

best LEARNS to simulate hard finite-state semiautomata from full state
supervision, within a fixed online-training budget?

"Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata" (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.10749):
online training with a freshly drawn batch at every step, AdamW, and a
per-position cross-entropy on the full state sequence. Their headline
finding: shallow non-recurrent networks learn o(T)-depth "shortcuts" to
solvable semiautomata, but accuracy on non-solvable word problems climbs
slowly with depth.

so no constant-depth parallel model can express it (unless TC0 = NC1), and
Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of State in State-Space Models"
(ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove diagonal linear recurrences (S4/Mamba
family) sit in L-uniform TC0 — they need depth growing with T on exactly
this problem.

constrains models whose serial computation depth does not grow with T.
A sequential RNN simulates ANY finite automaton by construction; both
reference papers use it as the trivial skyline (Liu et al. Fig. 5: a
1-layer LSTM reaches 100% on every task; Merrill et al. Fig. 3: a 1-layer

  2. an autograd-graph serial-depth probe: the longest path in the backward

automaton seed is masked before editable code sees the config: the model
must LEARN the automaton from sampled (input, state) streams. Hard-coding
or reconstructing any transition table inside the editable block is out of

    for these generator sets), sorted lexicographically, identity first (state 0).

    return out

_FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT = (nn.LSTM, nn.GRU, nn.RNN, nn.RNNBase,
                        nn.LSTMCell, nn.GRUCell, nn.RNNCell)


def check_no_recurrent_modules(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    for mod in model.modules():
        if isinstance(mod, _FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Recurrent module {type(mod).__name__} detected. This task "
                f"restricts the design space to parallel-time architectures: "
                f"a sequential RNN simulates any finite automaton by "
                f"construction (Liu et al. 2023 Fig. 5 report a 1-layer LSTM "
                f"at 100% on every task), so it is the excluded skyline here."
            )


def _graph_depth(output: torch.Tensor) -> int:
    """Longest path length in the autograd graph rooted at `output`."""
    root = output.grad_fn
    if root is None:
        return 0
    depth: dict = {}
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack[-1]
        if node in depth:
            stack.pop()
            continue
        pending = [
            child
            for child, _ in node.next_functions
            if child is not None and child not in depth
        ]
        if pending:
            stack.extend(pending)
        else:
            best = 0
            for child, _ in node.next_functions:
                if child is not None:
                    best = max(best, depth[child])
            depth[node] = 1 + best
            stack.pop()
    return depth[root]


def check_serial_depth(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                       config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Reject architectures whose serial depth grows with sequence length.

    Two dummy batches (lengths depth_probe_short and depth_probe_long) are
    forwarded and the longest autograd paths compared. Constant-depth models
    (attention, convolutions) and log-depth associative scans pass; per-token
    python recurrences add thousands of serial nodes and fail.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.train()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    depths = []
    for probe_len in (config.depth_probe_short, config.depth_probe_long):
        tokens = torch.randint(
            0, env_spec.alphabet_size, (2, probe_len),
            generator=gen, dtype=torch.long,
        ).to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, tokens, env_spec)
        depths.append(_graph_depth(logits))
    model.train(was_training)
    short_d, long_d = depths
    if long_d > short_d + config.depth_slack:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Serial-depth guard: autograd depth grew from {short_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_short}) to {long_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_long}); allowed slack is "
            f"{config.depth_slack}. Sequentially-recurrent computation is "
            f"not admissible in this task."
        )
    print(
        f"DEPTH_PROBE short={short_d} long={long_d} slack={config.depth_slack}",
        flush=True,
    )


@torch.no_grad()
def check_init_tripwire(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                        config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Abort if the *untrained* model already simulates the automaton.

    Chance accuracy is at most 1/24; an untrained learned model sits near
    chance, while a hard-coded (or table-reading) simulator is near 1.0.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20240819)
    correct, total = 0, 0
    for _ in range(4):
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, config.seq_len, gen)
        xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
        preds = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec).argmax(dim=-1)
        correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
        total += yb.numel()
    model.train(was_training)
    acc = correct / max(total, 1)
    print(f"INIT_TRIPWIRE acc={acc:.6f} threshold={config.init_tripwire_acc}",
          flush=True)
    if acc >= config.init_tripwire_acc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Init tripwire: untrained model reaches accuracy {acc:.4f} "
            f">= {config.init_tripwire_acc} (chance <= 1/24). Hard-coding "
            f"the automaton instead of learning it is out of contract."
        )

class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Default baseline: shallow GPT-2-style Transformer.

    Follows Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3: embedding dim 512, MLP width 512,
    8 heads, sinusoidal positional encodings; depth 1 is their shallowest
    configuration. Maps token ids [B, T] to state logits [B, T, Q].
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, n_heads: int = 8, n_layers: int = 1,
                 dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.register_buffer(
            "pos_table", sinusoidal_table(max_len, d_model), persistent=False)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=d_model,
            dropout=dropout, batch_first=True, activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)
        mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(max_len, max_len), diagonal=1).bool()
        self.register_buffer("causal_mask", mask, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids) + self.pos_table[:T].unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.encoder(x, mask=self.causal_mask[:T, :T], is_causal=True)
        return self.head(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the sequence model. Output: [B, T, num_states] logits."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        n_heads=8,
        n_layers=1,
        dropout=0.0,
    )


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict[str, float]:
    """AdamW hyperparameters (Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3: lr 3e-4, wd 1e-4)."""
    return {"lr": 3e-4, "wd": 1e-4, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Run the model on `input_ids` and return logits [B, T, num_states]."""
    return model(input_ids)

    words, evaluate on longer ones, as in PD-SSM's Table 3). The defaults are the
    fixed-length protocol: train and evaluate at `TaskConfig.seq_len`."""

    train_len_min: int | None = None   # per-step length ~ U[min, seq_len]
    eval_len_min: int | None = None    # per-batch length ~ U[min, max]
    eval_len_max: int | None = None
    metric: str = "all"                # scored accuracy: "all" positions | "final"
    early_stop: bool = True

    @property
    def extrapolation(self) -> bool:
        return self.eval_len_min is not None

def evaluate(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
             device: torch.device, eval_seed: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    correct, total, loss_sum = 0, 0, 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                                  config.seq_len, gen)
            xb = xb.to(device)
            yb = yb.to(device)
            logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                yb.reshape(-1),
            )
            preds = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
            total += yb.numel()
            loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return correct / max(total, 1), loss_sum / max(total, 1)


EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS = 4096   # 16 words x 256 tokens


def evaluate_lengths(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
                     protocol: LengthProtocol, device: torch.device,
                     eval_seed: int) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Accuracy on fresh words whose length is drawn per batch from
    U[eval_len_min, eval_len_max]: over all positions and at the final one."""
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    len_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed + 1)
    c_all = t_all = c_fin = t_fin = 0
    loss_sum = 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            length = int(torch.randint(protocol.eval_len_min,
                                       protocol.eval_len_max + 1, (1,),
                                       generator=len_gen))
            xb_all, yb_all = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, length, gen)
            # Memory only: long words are forwarded in sequence chunks of at most
            # EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS tokens (words are independent; same words, same
            # order, same counts). Lengths <= 256 are never chunked.
            step = max(1, EVAL_CHUNK_TOKENS // length)
            for i in range(0, xb_all.shape[0], step):
                xb = xb_all[i:i + step].to(device)
                yb = yb_all[i:i + step].to(device)
                logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
                loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                                       yb.reshape(-1))
                hit = logits.argmax(dim=-1) == yb
                c_all += hit.sum().item()
                t_all += yb.numel()
                c_fin += hit[:, -1].sum().item()
                t_fin += yb.shape[0]
                loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return {"acc_all": c_all / max(t_all, 1), "acc_final": c_fin / max(t_fin, 1),
            "loss": loss_sum / max(t_all, 1)}


def normalize_recipe(cfg: dict, config: TaskConfig) -> dict:
    """Optional training-recipe keys of `get_optimizer_config`'s dict.

    Defaults reproduce the plain recipe (constant lr, clip at
    `config.max_grad_norm`, one AdamW group), so a dict without these keys
    trains exactly as before. Keys:
      lr_schedule: "constant" | "warmup_cosine" (linear warmup over
                   warmup_frac * train_steps, then cosine to final_lr at the
                   last step; warmup_frac = 0 is torch's CosineAnnealingLR
                   with eta_min = final_lr)
      warmup_frac: float in [0, 1)            final_lr: float >= 0
      max_grad_norm: float > 0, or None for no clipping
      no_decay: list of parameter-name substrings trained with weight decay 0
    The step budget, batch size and evaluation are fixed.
    """
    schedule = cfg.get("lr_schedule", "constant")
    if schedule not in ("constant", "warmup_cosine"):
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown lr_schedule {schedule!r}.")
    warmup_frac = float(cfg.get("warmup_frac", 0.0))
    final_lr = float(cfg.get("final_lr", 0.0))
    if not 0.0 <= warmup_frac < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("warmup_frac must lie in [0, 1).")
    if final_lr < 0.0:
        raise ValueError("final_lr must be non-negative.")
    clip = cfg.get("max_grad_norm", config.max_grad_norm)
    if clip is not None:
        clip = float(clip)
        if clip <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError("max_grad_norm must be positive (or None).")
    no_decay = [str(s) for s in cfg.get("no_decay", ())]
    return {"lr_schedule": schedule, "warmup_frac": warmup_frac,
            "final_lr": final_lr, "max_grad_norm": clip,
            "no_decay": no_decay}


def scheduled_lr(step: int, total: int, max_lr: float, recipe: dict) -> float:
    """Learning rate for the optimizer step with 0-based index `step`."""
    warmup = int(recipe["warmup_frac"] * total)
    min_lr = recipe["final_lr"]
    if step < warmup:
        return max_lr * step / warmup
    if step >= total:
        return min_lr
    ratio = (step - warmup) / max(total - warmup, 1)
    return min_lr + 0.5 * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * ratio)) * (max_lr - min_lr)


def train(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device,
          protocol: LengthProtocol = LengthProtocol()) -> dict[str, float]:
    set_global_seed(config.seed)
    # Editable code sees the public spec and a config with the automaton
    # seed masked: the transition table must be learned, not reconstructed.
    masked_config = replace(config, dfa_seed=-1)
    model = build_model(env_spec, masked_config).to(device)
    check_no_recurrent_modules(model)
    check_serial_depth(model, env_spec, config, device)
    check_init_tripwire(model, env_spec, config, device)
    raw_opt_cfg = get_optimizer_config(masked_config)
    opt_cfg = normalize_optimizer_config(raw_opt_cfg)
    recipe = normalize_recipe(raw_opt_cfg, config)
    if recipe["no_decay"]:
        decay, no_decay = [], []
        for name, p in model.named_parameters():
            (no_decay if any(s in name for s in recipe["no_decay"])
             else decay).append(p)
        param_groups = [{"params": decay, "weight_decay": opt_cfg.wd},
                        {"params": no_decay, "weight_decay": 0.0}]
    else:
        param_groups = model.parameters()
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        param_groups,
        lr=opt_cfg.lr, betas=(opt_cfg.beta1, opt_cfg.beta2),
        weight_decay=opt_cfg.wd,
    )
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    print(
        f"MODEL_CONFIG env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"params={n_params}",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"OPT_CONFIG lr={opt_cfg.lr} wd={opt_cfg.wd} "
        f"beta1={opt_cfg.beta1} beta2={opt_cfg.beta2}",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"OPT_RECIPE lr_schedule={recipe['lr_schedule']} "
        f"warmup_frac={recipe['warmup_frac']} final_lr={recipe['final_lr']} "
        f"max_grad_norm={recipe['max_grad_norm']} "
        f"no_decay={','.join(recipe['no_decay']) or '-'}",
        flush=True,
    )

    train_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.seed * 7919 + 1)
    len_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.seed * 7919 + 2)
    stable_windows = 0
    last_train_acc = 0.0
    for step in range(1, config.train_steps + 1):
        model.train()
        length = config.seq_len
        if protocol.train_len_min is not None:
            length = int(torch.randint(protocol.train_len_min, config.seq_len + 1,
                                       (1,), generator=len_gen))
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, length, train_gen)
        xb = xb.to(device)
        yb = yb.to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
            yb.reshape(-1),
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        if recipe["max_grad_norm"] is not None:
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(),
                                           recipe["max_grad_norm"])
        if recipe["lr_schedule"] != "constant":
            lr_now = scheduled_lr(step - 1, config.train_steps, opt_cfg.lr,
                                  recipe)
            for group in optimizer.param_groups:
                group["lr"] = lr_now
        optimizer.step()

        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.train_steps:
            train_acc = (logits.argmax(dim=-1) == yb).float().mean().item()
            last_train_acc = train_acc
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS step={step} loss={loss.item():.6f} "
                f"train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            if train_acc >= config.early_stop_acc:
                stable_windows += 1
            else:
                stable_windows = 0
            if protocol.early_stop and stable_windows >= config.early_stop_windows:
                print(f"EARLY_STOP step={step} train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                      flush=True)
                break

    chance = 1.0 / env_spec.num_states
    extra: dict[str, float] = {}
    if protocol.extrapolation:
        res = evaluate_lengths(model, env_spec, config, protocol, device,
                               eval_seed=config.seed * 100003 + 7)
        eval_acc = res["acc_final"] if protocol.metric == "final" else res["acc_all"]
        eval_loss = res["loss"]
        indist, _ = evaluate(model, env_spec, config, device,
                             eval_seed=config.seed * 100003 + 11)
        extra = {"acc_all": res["acc_all"], "acc_final": res["acc_final"],
                 "acc_train_len": indist}
    else:
        eval_acc, eval_loss = evaluate(model, env_spec, config, device,
                                       eval_seed=config.seed * 100003 + 7)
    # Rescale so that chance level (1/|Q|) pins to 0.
    score = max(0.0, (eval_acc - chance) / (1.0 - chance))
    return {
        "test_accuracy": eval_acc,
        "test_loss": eval_loss,
        "score": score,
        "last_train_acc": last_train_acc,
        "num_params": float(n_params),
        **extra,
    }


def resolve_device(arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

def main() -> None:
    # The run script mints a per-run nonce and passes it here; the one scored
    # line carries it and the parser accepts exactly one line bearing it, so a
    # stray or forged `TEST_METRICS` print is not a score.
    import os as _os
    nonce = _os.environ.pop("MLSB_NONCE", "")
    args = parse_args()
    config = TaskConfig(env_name=args.env, seed=args.seed)
    if args.seq_len is not None:
        config = replace(config, seq_len=args.seq_len)
    if args.train_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, train_steps=args.train_steps)
    if args.batch_size is not None:
        config = replace(config, batch_size=args.batch_size)
    if args.eval_batches is not None:
        config = replace(config, eval_batches=args.eval_batches)
    config = maybe_apply_smoke(config, args.smoke)

    protocol = LengthProtocol(
        train_len_min=args.train_len_min, eval_len_min=args.eval_len_min,
        eval_len_max=args.eval_len_max, metric=args.eval_metric,
        early_stop=not args.no_early_stop)
    if (protocol.eval_len_min is None) != (protocol.eval_len_max is None):
        raise ValueError("--eval-len-min and --eval-len-max go together.")
    if protocol.extrapolation and not (
            1 <= protocol.eval_len_min <= protocol.eval_len_max
            <= max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long)):

def _delta_rule(q, k, v, beta, chunk: int = 64):

    S_t = (I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) S_{t-1} + beta_t k_t v_t^T,  o_t = K^-0.5 q_t^T S_t,
    S_0 = 0. Chunk-wise WY form (fp32 inside); the chunk-state carry is an inclusive
    Hillis-Steele scan (log depth).

        k = F.pad(k, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, pad))

    M = torch.cat([torch.cat([A, Bc], -1), eye_d[K:].expand(B, H, N, V, D)], -2)

    offset = 1

    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, hidden_ratio: int = 4):

    """fla_mod DeltaNetForCausalLM, hidden 128, 4 heads, no conv, 5 layers, [-1, 1]."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, hidden_size: int = 128,
                 num_layers: int = 5, num_heads: int = 4, norm_eps: float = 1e-6,
                 sigmoid_scale: float = 2.0, initializer_range: float = 0.02):
        super().__init__()
        self.bos_id = vocab_size                  # tokenizer's [BOS], prepended
        self.model = _DeltaNetModel(vocab_size + 1, hidden_size, num_layers,
                                    num_heads, norm_eps, sigmoid_scale)

        # initialised are skipped): N(0, 0.02) for embeddings / MLP / head, then the
        # prenorm rescale divides down_proj by sqrt(2 L).

        nn.init.normal_(self.lm_head.weight, std=initializer_range)

            nn.init.normal_(block.mlp.down_proj.weight, std=initializer_range)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """DeltaNet[-1,1] (5L): hidden 128, 4 heads, no short conv (Grazzi et al. App. E.2.1)."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
                               num_states=env_spec.num_states)


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict:
    """App. E.2.1: AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0.01, clip 1.0 (driver default), constant."""
    return {"lr": 1e-4, "wd": 0.01, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    return model(input_ids)

def _interleave(seqs):

    b, t = stacked.shape[:2]
    return stacked.reshape(b, t * len(seqs), *stacked.shape[3:])

    q, k, v, beta = q.float(), k.float(), v.float(), beta.float()

    k = k * torch.rsqrt((k * k).sum(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)

        beta = F.pad(beta, (0, 0, 0, pad))

    kb, vb = k * beta, v * beta
    eye_c = torch.eye(chunk, device=q.device, dtype=q.dtype)
    L = eye_c + torch.tril(kb @ k.transpose(-1, -2), diagonal=-1)
    w = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(L, kb, upper=False, unitriangular=True)
    u = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(L, vb, upper=False, unitriangular=True)

    M = torch.cat([torch.cat([A, Bc], -1), eye_d[K:].expand(B, H, N, V, D)], -2)

    offset = 1

        M = torch.bmm(M, torch.cat([eye_d.expand(offset * G, D, D),
                                    M[:(N - offset) * G]], 0))
        offset *= 2
    S_end = M[:, :K, K:].reshape(N, B, H, K, V).permute(1, 2, 0, 3, 4)  # S_c (S_0 = 0)
    S0 = torch.cat([S_end.new_zeros(B, H, 1, K, V), S_end[:, :, :-1]], 2)  # entry state

            ks.append(F.silu(self.k_projs[i](x)))
            vs.append(F.silu(self.v_projs[i](x)))
            beta = self.b_projs[i](x).sigmoid()
            if self.allow_neg_eigval:

            betas.append(beta)
        q = F.silu(self.q_proj(x))
        q = _interleave([torch.zeros_like(q)] * (self.num_householder - 1) + [q])
        k, v, beta = _interleave(ks), _interleave(vs), _interleave(betas)
        b, t = q.shape[:2]
        q, k, v = (z.reshape(b, t, self.num_heads, -1) for z in (q, k, v))
        o = _delta_rule(q, k, v, beta)
        o = o[:, self.num_householder - 1::self.num_householder]
        o = self.o_norm(o)
        return self.o_proj(o.reshape(o.shape[0], o.shape[1], -1))

        h = self.attn(self.attn_norm(h))

            [_DeltaProductBlock(hidden_size, norm_eps, **attn_kwargs)
             for _ in range(num_layers)])

Architecture family: Gu & Dao, "Mamba" (arXiv:2312.00752) / gated linear
recurrences. Negative theory: Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of
State in State-Space Models" (ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove that
diagonal (input-dependent) linear recurrences sit in L-uniform TC0 and so
cannot express non-solvable group word problems such as S5 at any width;
empirically they need depth growing with sequence length. This baseline
pins that prediction on the leaderboard: competitive on the random-DFA
environments (whose random transformations contain much rank-collapsing,
shortcut-friendly structure) and near the floor on `s5-word`.

The recurrence h_t = a_t * h_{t-1} + (1 - a_t) * v_t is computed with a
Hillis-Steele parallel scan (log2(T) combine rounds), so its serial depth
is O(log T) and it passes the task's parallel-time guard — its failure on
S5 is expressivity, not the guard.

class _GatedDiagScanBlock(nn.Module):
    """h_t = a_t * h_{t-1} + (1 - a_t) * v_t via a log-depth parallel scan."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.a_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        u = self.norm(x)
        a = torch.sigmoid(self.a_proj(u))       # decay gate in (0, 1)
        h = (1.0 - a) * self.v_proj(u)          # input contribution
        # Inclusive Hillis-Steele scan: ceil(log2 T) combine rounds, each a
        # constant number of parallel ops, so serial depth is O(log T).
        T = x.shape[1]
        offset = 1
        while offset < T:
            a_prev = F.pad(a, (0, 0, offset, 0), value=1.0)[:, :T]
            h_prev = F.pad(h, (0, 0, offset, 0), value=0.0)[:, :T]
            h = h + a * h_prev
            a = a * a_prev
            offset *= 2
        return x + self.out_proj(h)

            nn.Linear(2 * d_model, d_model),

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids)
        for block in self.blocks:
            x = block(x)
        x = x + self.mlp(x)
        return self.head(x)

"""Looped Transformer baseline for theory-semiautomata.

Weight-shared depth recurrence in the spirit of Giannou et al. 2023
"Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers" (arXiv:2301.13196) and the
depth-vs-difficulty ladder of Liu et al. 2023 (arXiv:2210.10749, Thm. 1:
O(log T) attention depth suffices for any semiautomaton, and no constant
depth suffices for non-solvable ones unless TC0 = NC1). One shared
encoder block is applied 8 times, giving effective depth 8 at roughly
1/8 of the deep baseline's parameters — it tests whether the iterated
structure of automaton composition can be learned with tied weights.
"""

_FILE = "pytorch-examples/theory_semiautomata/custom_strategy.py"

_CONTENT = '''\
class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Looped Transformer: one shared encoder layer applied n_loops times."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, n_heads: int = 8, n_loops: int = 8,
                 dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_loops = n_loops
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.register_buffer(
            "pos_table", sinusoidal_table(max_len, d_model), persistent=False)
        self.block = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=d_model,
            dropout=dropout, batch_first=True, activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.final_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)
        mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(max_len, max_len), diagonal=1).bool()
        self.register_buffer("causal_mask", mask, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids) + self.pos_table[:T].unsqueeze(0)
        mask = self.causal_mask[:T, :T]
        for _ in range(self.n_loops):
            x = self.block(x, src_mask=mask, is_causal=True)
        x = self.final_norm(x)
        return self.head(x)

    """Looped Transformer: shared block, 8 loops, d_model=512, 8 heads."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        n_heads=8,

"""Mamba[-1, 1], 5 layers (Grazzi et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv:2411.12537).

PROVENANCE -- faithful, no deviations.
  Source: https://github.com/automl/unlocking_state_tracking @ 68f8e5fc6d25043d4e6a1fc169b58281c9e01d12
    mixer   mamba_dev/mamba_ssm/modules/mamba_simple.py (Mamba, with
            positive_and_negative_associative_scan=True)
    scan    mamba_dev/csrc/selective_scan_positive_and_negative/*.cuh and the reference
            mamba_dev/mamba_ssm/ops/selective_scan_interface.py:selective_scan_ref:
            deltaA = 2 * exp(delta * A) - 1  (eigenvalues in (-1, 1)), deltaB_u = delta*B*u
    init    mamba_dev/mamba_ssm/models/mixer_seq_simple.py:_init_weights (n_residuals 1)
  Model wrapper: the S5 experiments ran on Merrill et al.'s word-problem code
    (https://github.com/jopetty/word-problem @ 8f910f92, src/main.py:train_mamba), whose
    model is sfirah's MambaTokenClassifier (https://github.com/jopetty/sfirah @ 30b5a873,
    sfirah/ssm.py): embedding -> n_layers x mamba Block (Add -> LayerNorm -> Mixer,
    eps 1e-5, no fused add-norm, residual not in fp32) -> final LayerNorm -> linear head
    with bias (train_mamba default bias=True); _init_weights applied before the head is
    created.
  Setting: the paper's S5 configuration (Sec. 5.2, App. E.2.1, Fig. 4 legend
    "Mamba [-1,1] (5L)"): embedding dimension 128, 5 layers, mixer defaults (d_state 16,
    d_conv 4, expand 2, dt_rank ceil(128/16) = 8). Recipe (App. E.2.1; train_mamba
    defaults agree): AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0.01, gradient clipping 1.0 (the
    driver's default clip), constant lr.
  Precision: the S5 pipeline was not released; following the authors' released
    state-tracking pipeline (xlstm/experiments/parity_mamba_2.yaml: weight_precision
    float32, amp_precision bfloat16) -- fp32 weights under bf16 autocast; the selective
    scan computes in fp32 as in the CUDA kernel.
  Kernel: the CUDA selective scan (not in the image) is computed in plain torch as the
    same linear recurrence h_t = deltaA_t * h_{t-1} + deltaB_u_t (elementwise per
    channel/state) evaluated by a log-depth Hillis-Steele scan instead of the kernel's
    chunked block scan -- the same recurrence, different association order. Verified
    against selective_scan_ref (sequential, copied from the repo) and against the
    reference Mamba module's non-fused path (weights loaded by name): see NOTES.md.
  I/O: the word-problem tokenizer prepends [BOS]; done here with one extra embedding row
    (id = alphabet_size), BOS output dropped; head maps to the task's states.
"""

_CONTENT = '''\
class _MambaMixer(nn.Module):
    """mamba_ssm Mamba (mamba_simple.py) with the [-1, 1] selective scan."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, d_state: int = 16, d_conv: int = 4,
                 expand: int = 2, dt_min: float = 0.001, dt_max: float = 0.1,
                 dt_init_floor: float = 1e-4, dt_scale: float = 1.0,
                 conv_bias: bool = True, bias: bool = False):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_state = d_state
        self.d_inner = int(expand * d_model)
        self.dt_rank = math.ceil(d_model / 16)
        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, self.d_inner * 2, bias=bias)
        self.conv1d = nn.Conv1d(self.d_inner, self.d_inner, bias=conv_bias,
                                kernel_size=d_conv, groups=self.d_inner,
                                padding=d_conv - 1)
        self.x_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, self.dt_rank + d_state * 2, bias=False)
        self.dt_proj = nn.Linear(self.dt_rank, self.d_inner, bias=True)
        dt_init_std = self.dt_rank ** -0.5 * dt_scale
        nn.init.uniform_(self.dt_proj.weight, -dt_init_std, dt_init_std)
        dt = torch.exp(
            torch.rand(self.d_inner) * (math.log(dt_max) - math.log(dt_min))
            + math.log(dt_min)
        ).clamp(min=dt_init_floor)
        inv_dt = dt + torch.log(-torch.expm1(-dt))   # inverse softplus
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.dt_proj.bias.copy_(inv_dt)
        A = torch.arange(1, d_state + 1, dtype=torch.float32).repeat(self.d_inner, 1)
        self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A))      # S4D-real init
        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.d_inner))
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d_model, bias=bias)

    def forward(self, hidden_states):
        L = hidden_states.shape[1]
        x, z = self.in_proj(hidden_states).chunk(2, dim=-1)       # [B, L, Di]
        x = F.silu(self.conv1d(x.transpose(1, 2))[..., :L]).transpose(1, 2)
        dt, Bm, Cm = torch.split(self.x_proj(x),
                                 [self.dt_rank, self.d_state, self.d_state], dim=-1)
        dt = dt @ self.dt_proj.weight.t()                        # bias added in the scan
        # selective scan (fp32), delta_softplus=True, positive_and_negative=True
        u = x.float()
        delta = F.softplus(dt.float() + self.dt_proj.bias.float())
        A = -torch.exp(self.A_log.float())                       # [Di, N]
        dA = 2 * torch.exp(delta.unsqueeze(-1) * A) - 1          # [B, L, Di, N]
        h = delta.unsqueeze(-1) * Bm.float().unsqueeze(2) * u.unsqueeze(-1)
        offset = 1
        while offset < L:   # inclusive Hillis-Steele scan of h_t = dA_t h_{t-1} + dBu_t
            a_prev = torch.cat([torch.ones_like(dA[:, :offset]), dA[:, :-offset]], 1)
            h_prev = torch.cat([torch.zeros_like(h[:, :offset]), h[:, :-offset]], 1)
            h = h + dA * h_prev
            dA = dA * a_prev
            offset *= 2
        y = (h * Cm.float().unsqueeze(2)).sum(-1) + u * self.D.float()
        y = y * F.silu(z.float())
        return self.out_proj(y.to(x.dtype))


class _MambaBlock(nn.Module):
    """mamba_ssm Block: Add -> LayerNorm -> Mixer, returns (hidden, residual)."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, eps: float):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model, eps=eps)
        self.mixer = _MambaMixer(d_model)

    def forward(self, hidden_states, residual):
        residual = hidden_states + residual if residual is not None else hidden_states
        hidden_states = self.norm(residual.to(dtype=self.norm.weight.dtype))
        return self.mixer(hidden_states), residual


class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """sfirah MambaTokenClassifier: d_model 128, 5 layers, [-1, 1] scan."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, d_model: int = 128,
                 n_layers: int = 5, layer_norm_eps: float = 1e-5):
        super().__init__()
        self.bos_id = vocab_size                  # tokenizer's [BOS], prepended
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size + 1, d_model)
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
            [_MambaBlock(d_model, layer_norm_eps) for _ in range(n_layers)])
        self.norm_f = nn.LayerNorm(d_model, eps=layer_norm_eps)
        # mixer_seq_simple._init_weights(n_layer=n_layers), applied by sfirah's Mamba
        # before the head exists: Linear biases zeroed (dt_proj.bias kept), embedding
        # N(0, 0.02), out_proj kaiming_uniform(a=sqrt 5) / sqrt(n_layers).
        nn.init.normal_(self.embedding.weight, std=0.02)
        for layer in self.layers:
            for mod in (layer.mixer.in_proj, layer.mixer.x_proj, layer.mixer.out_proj):
                if mod.bias is not None:
                    nn.init.zeros_(mod.bias)
            nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(layer.mixer.out_proj.weight, a=math.sqrt(5))
            with torch.no_grad():
                layer.mixer.out_proj.weight /= math.sqrt(n_layers)
        self.cl_head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states, bias=True)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bos = torch.full_like(input_ids[:, :1], self.bos_id)
        with torch.autocast(device_type=input_ids.device.type, dtype=torch.bfloat16):
            x = self.embedding(torch.cat([bos, input_ids], dim=1))
            residual = None
            for layer in self.layers:
                x, residual = layer(x, residual)
            residual = x + residual
            x = self.norm_f(residual.to(dtype=self.norm_f.weight.dtype))
            logits = self.cl_head(x)
        return logits.float()[:, 1:]          # autocast runs the loss in fp32


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Mamba[-1,1] (5L), d_model 128 (Grazzi et al. App. E.2.1)."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
                               num_states=env_spec.num_states)


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict:
    """App. E.2.1: AdamW lr 1e-4, weight decay 0.01, clip 1.0 (driver default), constant."""
    return {"lr": 1e-4, "wd": 0.01, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    return model(input_ids)

    batch with optimizer.zero_grad() in between; with torch >= 2.0 zero_grad sets grads to

  Recurrence: pdssm.py runs h_t = A(u_t) h_{t-1} + B u_t, h_0 = e_1, with a python loop
    over time (the README: "implemented in a fully recurrent way"); the task's
    parallel-time guard rejects that, and the authors' own parallel version is the JAX
    associative scan (time_series_JAX/models/PDSSM.py). Here the same recurrence is a
    log-depth Hillis-Steele scan over the dense complex transition matrices
    (D(u_t) * P(u_t), with P's straight-through one-hot exactly as in pdssm.py, so the
    forward values and the autograd graph through the soft column are the reference's) --
    the same linear recurrence, different association order. Verified against the
    sequential reference module (weights loaded by name): see NOTES.md.
  I/O: return_all_outputs=True (per-position outputs); the readout maps to the task's
    states; the formal-language pipeline feeds raw tokens (no BOS).
"""

_FILE = "pytorch-examples/theory_semiautomata/custom_strategy.py"

_CONTENT = '''\
class _PDBlock(nn.Module):
    """pdssm.py PD_Block (post-LN block), recurrence by a parallel scan."""

    def __init__(self, embed_size: int, hidden_size: int, dictionary_size: int = 8,
                 hidden_D_multiple: int = 2, dropout_rate: float = 0.01):
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden_size = hidden_size
        self.embed_size = embed_size
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(embed_size)
        self.drop = nn.Dropout(p=dropout_rate)
        self.D_magnitude_generator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_size, hidden_D_multiple * hidden_size), nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_D_multiple * hidden_size, hidden_size), nn.Sigmoid())
        self.D_phase_generator = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(embed_size, hidden_D_multiple * hidden_size), nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_D_multiple * hidden_size, hidden_size), nn.Sigmoid())
        self.S = nn.Linear(embed_size, dictionary_size, bias=False)
        self.A_dict = nn.Parameter(
            torch.randn(hidden_size, hidden_size, dictionary_size) / math.sqrt(hidden_size))
        self.B_re = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(hidden_size, embed_size) / math.sqrt(2 * hidden_size))
        self.B_im = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(hidden_size, embed_size) / math.sqrt(2 * hidden_size))
        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(embed_size) / math.sqrt(embed_size))
        self.readout = nn.Linear(2 * embed_size, embed_size)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        Bsz, L, E = x.shape
        N = self.hidden_size
        selection_weights = F.softmax(self.S(x), dim=-1)                  # B L K
        M = torch.einsum("nmk,blk->blnm", self.A_dict, selection_weights)  # B L N N
        y_soft = F.softmax(M, dim=-1)
        y_hard = F.one_hot(torch.argmax(y_soft, dim=-1), num_classes=N)
        P = (y_hard - y_soft).detach() + y_soft                           # straight-through
        magnitudes_raw = self.D_magnitude_generator(x)
        magnitudes = torch.complex(magnitudes_raw, torch.zeros_like(magnitudes_raw))
        phases_raw = 2 * math.pi * self.D_phase_generator(x)
        phases = torch.exp(torch.complex(torch.zeros_like(phases_raw), phases_raw))
        A = (magnitudes * phases).unsqueeze(-1) * P                       # B L N N complex
        B_mat = torch.complex(self.B_re, self.B_im)
        b = torch.einsum("ne,ble->bln", B_mat, torch.complex(x, torch.zeros_like(x)))
        # h_t = A_t h_{t-1} + b_t from h_0 = e_1: fold h_0 into b_1, then an inclusive
        # Hillis-Steele scan over the affine maps (A_t, b_t) (log depth).
        b = torch.cat([b[:, :1] + A[:, :1, :, 0], b[:, 1:]], dim=1)
        eye = torch.eye(N, dtype=A.dtype, device=A.device)
        offset = 1
        while offset < L:
            b_prev = torch.cat([torch.zeros_like(b[:, :offset]), b[:, :-offset]], 1)
            b = (A @ b_prev.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1) + b
            if 2 * offset < L:
                A_prev = torch.cat([eye.expand(Bsz, offset, N, N), A[:, :-offset]], 1)
                A = A @ A_prev
            offset *= 2
        hidden_states = b
        linear_readout_re_im = torch.cat((hidden_states.real, hidden_states.imag), dim=-1)
        output = self.readout(self.drop(linear_readout_re_im)) + self.D * x
        return self.norm(output)


class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """pdssm.py PD with return_all_outputs=True."""

    def __init__(self, output_size: int, input_size: int, state_size: int = 128,
                 embed_size: int = 128, dictionary_size: int = 32, num_layers: int = 1,
                 dropout_rate: float = 0.01):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_layers = num_layers
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            _PDBlock(embed_size=embed_size, hidden_size=state_size,
                     dictionary_size=dictionary_size, dropout_rate=dropout_rate)
            for _ in range(num_layers))
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(input_size, embed_size)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(embed_size, output_size)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.embedding(x)
        for i in range(self.num_layers):
            x = self.blocks[i](x)
        return self.readout(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """PD-SSM: 1 layer, K = 32, state 128 (Table 3 group setting)."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(output_size=env_spec.num_states,
                               input_size=env_spec.alphabet_size)


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict:
    """train.py: AdamW lr 2e-3, wd 0.01 (0 on the embedding), 10% warmup + cosine to
    1e-5, no clipping."""
    return {"lr": 2e-3, "wd": 0.01, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999,
            "lr_schedule": "warmup_cosine", "warmup_frac": 0.1, "final_lr": 1e-5,
            "max_grad_norm": None, "no_decay": ["embedding"]}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    return model(input_ids)
'''

"""NULL baseline for theory-semiautomata: a position-wise (bag-of-one-token) MLP.

This is the declared null (``"null": true`` in config.json).  It honours the
task's I/O contract exactly -- ``build_model`` returns an nn.Module mapping
token ids [B, T] to per-position state logits [B, T, Q], ``get_optimizer_config``
returns the same AdamW recipe as the reference baselines, ``forward_logits``
is the identity wrapper -- and it passes both fixed guards (no recurrent
module; its serial depth is independent of T, so the autograd-depth probe is
flat).  What it cannot do is the one thing the task measures: **track state**.

Its receptive field is a single position.  The logits at position t are a
function of x_t alone, with no mixing across positions of any kind -- no
attention, no convolution, no scan.  The state of a semiautomaton at
position t is the left product delta(...delta(q_0, x_0)..., x_t), so the
best any position-wise map can do is predict the mode of the pushforward
of the state distribution under delta(., x_t):

  * on the two `random_dfa` settings delta(., a) is a random *function*
    on |Q| states, so its image is unbalanced and the modal preimage gives
    a small but nonzero edge over chance;
  * on `s5-word` every letter is a *permutation* of the 120 states, so the
    pushforward of a near-uniform state distribution is exactly uniform and
    the null is pinned at chance -- i.e. score ~ 0 on precisely the setting
    Liu et al. 2023 and Merrill et al. 2024 use to separate architectures.

That graded floor is the point: it says how much of the label is readable
off the current symbol without simulating anything, so a model's score
above it is the part attributable to state tracking.

Width is matched to the reference Transformer (d_model = 512, MLP width
512, GELU) so this is a null by *architecture*, not by width: the model is
free to spend all of that capacity on the map x_t -> q_t and still cannot
express the task, because the information it needs is at the other
positions and no path in its graph reaches them.  Measured on s5-word,
seed 42: DEPTH_PROBE short=15 long=15 (flat in T, so the parallel-time
guard passes), INIT_TRIPWIRE acc=0.0080, params=593016.
"""

_FILE = "pytorch-examples/theory_semiautomata/custom_strategy.py"

_CONTENT = '''\
class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """NULL: position-wise MLP -- the logits at t depend only on x_t.

    No attention, no convolution, no scan, no recurrence: there is no path
    in this graph from position t' != t to the output at position t, so the
    model cannot track the automaton's state at all.  Width matches the
    reference Transformer (d_model = 512, MLP width 512) so the floor is
    architectural rather than a capacity handicap.
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, hidden: int = 512):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
            nn.Linear(d_model, hidden),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden, d_model),
            nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
        )
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # [B, T] -> [B, T, d_model]; every position is processed on its own.
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids)
        x = x + self.mlp(x)
        return self.head(x)

    """Construct the sequence model. Output: [B, T, num_states] logits."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
